notes: The breadboard image is drawn with rows j-f in the upper half and a-e in the lower half; the catalogue's bank 'b' (rows f-j) is therefore the upper half and bank 't' (rows a-e) the lower half.
The button straddles the centre gap at columns 4 and 6. Column 4 is side 1 (5V) and column 6 is side 2 (pin 2 and the resistor).
Rail hole numbers are estimated from their positions in the image. The red wire goes to the lower rail row, which I called bp. The black rail row is bn.
The tutorial text also mentions an LED on pin 13. It is the Uno's built-in LED, so no external LED is added.
The resistor is 10k, as given in the manual and the schematic.
The Arduino GND wire goes to the GND pin in the power header, which I mapped to GND.1.
